slot.brief: Give a target ether and ask which alkyl halide + alkoxide combination is correct, including one option that fails due to elimination with a secondary/tertiary halide.

stem: Which pair is most suitable for preparing ethoxycyclopentane by Williamson synthesis?

verdicts.working: Use the primary alkyl halide in the SN2 step: sodium cyclopentoxide reacts with bromoethane to form ethoxycyclopentane.

working:
$\text{C}_5\text{H}_9\text{O}^-+\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Br}\rightarrow\text{C}_5\text{H}_9\text{OC}_2\text{H}_5+\text{Br}^-$
Primary bromoethane undergoes $S_\text{N}2$ substitution with cyclopentoxide.

Independent check: Use the primary alkyl halide in the SN2 step: sodium cyclopentoxide reacts with bromoethane to form ethoxycyclopentane.
solution:
Williamson synthesis proceeds by an $S_\text{N}2$ reaction, so use the primary alkyl halide, bromoethane.
$$\mathrm{C_5H_9O^- + C_2H_5Br \longrightarrow C_5H_9OC_2H_5 + Br^-}$$
Thus, sodium cyclopentoxide and bromoethane form ethoxycyclopentane.
